messages:
sam: quick q — ruby SDK isn't auto-refreshing tokens like node/python. rails sample-app Sidekiq job gets 401s after idle and fails instead of refreshing. anyone else hit this?

priya: yep saw customer report. which sdk version?

sam: 0.12.3. repro: create client with `Client.new(access_token: token, retry: true)` then long-running job hits 401 and no refresh.

leo: node/python accept token provider callbacks so SDK can call them. ruby still treats access_token as static in many code paths. there was a WIP PR?

tina: PR #812 adds `token_provider:` option (proc returning token). left review notes: need retry-on-401 hook and ensure auth middleware runs on each retry. also add tests.

sam: Sidekiq job retries are noisy; prefer SDK transparently refreshes before failing.

priya: remember Faraday middleware ordering — if retry runs before auth, refreshed header won't be applied. auth middleware must set Authorization per attempt.

leo: implement AuthMiddleware that calls token_provider per-request, RetryMiddleware that on 401 invokes token_provider once and retries one time with jittered backoff. match node/python semantics.

tina: suggested code sketch in PR comment: `client = Client.new(token_provider: -> { fetch_fresh_token }, retry: { max: 3, backoff: :exponential })` and internal ordering Auth -> Retry. asked for integration test simulating expiry to assert single refresh call.

sam: i'll add a failing test in sample-app-rails Sidekiq worker to catch regressions.

ci-bot: CI for PR #812: unit tests queued.

priya: docs note: update README quickstart to show token_provider example and call out sidekiq pattern. onboarding questions keep coming from folks using static tokens in long-running jobs.

leo: add CHANGELOG entry: "Ruby SDK: token_provider callable for on-demand refresh; aligns behavior with node/python; deprecate static token in 6 months."

sam: i'll open ISSUE to track deprecation and ping CS for affected customers.

ci-bot: PR #812 tests passed at 1819876578. merging after maintainer approval.

priya: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
